selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is this warning about?
questions.answer: It is about why this book can be hard to understand.

questions.question: Does the passage give only a warning, or also some encouragement?
questions.answer: It gives both warning and encouragement.

questions.question: How many reasons are given for the difficulty?
questions.answer: Five.

questions.question: What is one clue from the first cause that the book is personal in style?
questions.answer: It was written from the writer’s own observations.

questions.question: What is the second reason the book may be hard?
questions.answer: The topics are very big, deep, and long.

questions.question: Why might a proof need many beginning parts first?
questions.answer: Because the truth being shown is large and needs setup.

questions.question: In the fourth reason, what makes the discussion longer?
questions.answer: Many proofs and signs are included.

questions.question: What did he not do to the first draft?
questions.answer: He did not revise it.

questions.question: What two language-related details are mentioned at the end?
questions.answer: Some parts were in Arabic, and one fully Arabic section was made separate.

questions.question: What is the main message of the warning at the beginning?
questions.answer: Not everyone will understand everything, but everyone can gain something.

questions.question: What picture is used to help us understand this idea?
questions.answer: A person in a garden picking only some fruit.

questions.question: What was not his main goal in writing?
questions.answer: Matching the ideas of other people.

questions.question: In the second cause, what three words best describe the topics?
questions.answer: Wide, deep, and long.

questions.question: What is the third reason the book may be hard?
questions.answer: One sentence may become very long to protect one whole truth.

questions.question: In the fifth reason, when did these ideas come to the writer?
questions.answer: During Ramadan.

questions.question: Which cause shows that the writer was not trying to write for everybody’s level?
questions.answer: The first cause.

questions.question: What final detail shows why some readers might struggle with the book’s language?
questions.answer: Parts of it were in Arabic.

questions.question: What kind of note is this passage: a story, a warning, or a set of rules?
questions.answer: A warning.

questions.question: Does the passage say the book is made for only one kind of reader?
questions.answer: No. It is for different readers with different levels.

questions.question: How many reasons are given for the book being hard to understand?
questions.answer: Five reasons.

questions.question: What is the first cause about?
questions.answer: The book comes from the writer’s own understanding and experience.

questions.question: Why can such a subject be hard for some readers?
questions.answer: It is very broad and deep.

questions.question: What is the fourth reason the book may be hard?
questions.answer: It gives many proofs and evidences.

questions.question: Why did he not fix and rearrange the writing later?
questions.answer: He felt he should not change it by his own thoughts.
